claims.text: A thin, uniform ALD-deposited Al2O3 coating on zirconium-alloy cladding will reduce high-temperature oxidation relative to uncoated cladding.
The coated cladding will retain properties required for in-service use.
ALD can produce a continuous, dense, adherent, nanometer-scale Al2O3 barrier on zirconium-alloy cladding.
The ALD-deposited alumina layer acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier with low oxygen permeability.
Limiting oxygen ingress through the alumina layer slows oxidation kinetics in the underlying zirconium alloy.
The alumina coating can slow oxidation without compromising the mechanical integrity of the zirconium-alloy cladding.
Relative to bare cladding, coated cladding will develop a thinner oxide scale under the same high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Relative to bare cladding, coated cladding will exhibit lower oxidation-associated weight gain under the same high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
The coated cladding will continue to meet service-performance criteria after high-temperature oxidation exposure.
Oxidizing exposure at approximately 1000–1200 degrees Celsius is representative of accident scenarios relevant to zirconium-alloy fuel cladding.
The oxidation benefit requires the alumina coating to remain adherent and substantially free of cracking or delamination through thermal transients.
An overly thick or non-uniform alumina coating may fail to provide the predicted improvement.
Adverse effects of the coating on thermal conductivity or other service-related properties may negate its suitability.
The magnitude of oxidation reduction may vary with coating quality and test conditions.
